_frame_plan_note: 960 frames at 30 fps; shot boundaries sit in the gaps between the measured spoken windows of the first preflight (0.10-4.44, 4.93-9.16, 9.65-14.04, 14.54-19.40, 19.90-25.88, 26.38-31.61 s).

shots.visual_proof: Slow motion from beside the bed entrance with a red BRAKES FAILED warning over the speed read-out for the first seconds: the truck arrives close at 90 km/h, its tyres dig into the stones and gravel and dust spray up; then a dolly ahead of the truck and a side-on view of the rear wheels.
shots.narration_en: This truck has lost its brakes, and it is about to plow into a bed of loose gravel.

shots.visual_proof: Macro at the drive wheels: the tyres sit below the surface of the gravel and push a wave of stones aside while the read-out falls.
shots.narration_en: Every wheel sinks into the stones, and digging through them drains the truck's speed.

shots.visual_proof: A cutaway slice of the bed (cutaway device): a wheel rolls across the loose rounded stones, sinks into them and throws stones ahead of it, seen in an orbit and then close on the cut face.
shots.narration_en: The bed is just a thick layer of round stones, piled deep and left loose.

shots.visual_proof: Raised tracking view from behind: the truck keeps slowing while a read-out compares gravel drag (0.25 g) with pavement (0.01 g, assumed values).
shots.narration_en: Loose gravel drags at about a quarter of the truck's weight, twenty-five times more than pavement.

shots.visual_proof: Straight-down view with a green bar to where the truck actually stops (about 133 m) while a second, orange truck (the same truck coasting on pavement at constant speed, an illustration) keeps running down the paved lane and out of the picture; the orange bar runs off the end of the picture for the paved coast.
shots.narration_en: On pavement this truck would coast over three kilometers; the gravel stops it in about one hundred thirty meters.

shots.visual_proof: Wide, low and raised views of the ramp branching from a highway with a truck passing in the next lane; the last two seconds return to the opening camera with a truck arriving again, ending one frame before the film's first frame so the Short loops.
shots.narration_en: That is why steep mountain roads have ramps like this, waiting beside the highway for the next runaway truck.

first_three_seconds.note: Counts physical events becoming true and visible, not cuts or camera moves.

_edit_order_note: Shot order follows retention evidence from an earlier episode (steepest viewer loss at 3.5-6 s when the picture went from an event to an explanation; second loss at an 'and that is why' ending): the action macro follows the hook, the static cutaway moves to third and the ending loops back to the first frame.
